thread:
ida: Heads-up — received escalation from AcmeMaps about p99 spikes on their Dedicated pool (pool-id: dp-42). Reported latency started ~2026-03-14T10:02Z and has been intermittent since. Customer says some requests >10s.

leo: Copy. Do we have metrics?

ida: Quick numbers from metrics cluster: p95 jumped from ~1.2s -> ~2.9s, p99 spikes up to 12s over the last 40m. Error rate still low (~0.2%). Throughput steady.

autoscale-bot: [alert] dedicated-pool/dp-42 provisioner throttle detected — 429/ProvisioningThrottle events increasing (rate: 4/min)

raj: Sounds like scale-up lag + provisioning throttle. Any recent config changes for dp-42?

ida: No config change in the last 24h. Last deploy of runtime two days ago — nothing touching autoscaler. I checked pool config: min_replicas=2, max_replicas=20, scale_up_rate=2/min.

maria: From customer: "We hit heavy tail on long requests after batch job started routing a lot of long-sequence requests. Some requests timeout at our side after 15s."

raj: OK could be a thundering-herd when many long-seq requests cause concurrent cold starts. Can someone repro?

ida: Repro steps I used locally (from operator workstation):
```
# simulate customer payloads
for i in {1..30}; do 
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\
    -H "Authorization: Bearer REPRO_KEY" \\
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\
    -d '{"model":"llama-2-13b", "input":"'"Long sequence test ${i}"'", "max_tokens":1024}' &
done
wait
```
Observed a backlog and several requests queued; new instances took ~35-50s to become ready (GPU cold start + image pull).

leo: Did you see image pull times or instance preemption?

ida: Image pull slow in a few samples: ~20s to pull container. Cloud logs show a burst of api rate-limits to the provisioning API — looks like we're throttled by the cloud provider (ProvisioningThrottle). Also saw kubelet CNI delays in a few nodes.

raj: That matches autoscale-bot. If cloud is throttling instance create, our scale-up per-minute limit makes it worse. We need a mitigation ASAP to reduce customer impact.

ida: Short-term mitigation options I propose:
- bump min_replicas for dp-42 from 2 -> 6 so there are warm instances (manual immediate).
- temporarily increase scale_up_rate to 6/min or the equivalent to allow faster ramp (careful).
- create an emergency warm pool (pre-warmed instances) in the same region for customers with long-seq SLAs.
- route AcmeMaps to a fallback smaller model (13b -> 7b) to reduce cold start work and latency.

maria: Customer accepts temporary fallback to 7b if it lowers p99. They want updates every 15m.

leo: I'll draft the customer update. Ida/raj: can you run the config changes and verify?

ida: On it. Executing: `rdctl pools update dp-42 --min-replicas 6`

[system logs pasted by ida]
```
INFO 2026-03-14T10:28:12Z pool-controller: updating min_replicas dp-42 -> 6
WARN 2026-03-14T10:28:20Z provisioner: provisioning request queued (rate-limit hit)
INFO 2026-03-14T10:29:03Z node-launch: started instance i-0abcd1234
INFO 2026-03-14T10:29:50Z node-ready: instance i-0abcd1234 ready, warmed cache
```

ida: After bumping min_replicas we immediately saw two warm nodes come up but they took ~45s. p99 dropped to ~3.8s within 2m and then stabilised to ~2.6s after more nodes were ready.

raj: Nice. Still need permanent fix — cloud provisioning throttle is the root cause. Possible actions: request higher provisioning quota with provider, implement exponential jitter on our provisioning requests to avoid bursts, and introduce local warm pool per region.

ida: Filed infra ticket INF-5421 requesting increased instance launch quota and exemption for autoscaler burst. Also opened follow-up to add jitter and progressive backoff tuning: AUTOSCALE-298.

leo: Customer update sent: "We've temporarily increased warm capacity for your Dedicated pool and are monitoring. We're also offering a fallback model for immediate relief. Will follow up with a root cause and timeline." :thumbsup:

maria: Thanks team. Can we capture repro artifacts for postmortem?

ida: Pushing logs and the curl script to the thread: link https://internal.redwood/sre/1845678901/logs (priv repo). Key traceback: `provisioning API 429 -> autoscaler backoff double -> queue length climbs`

raj: Also note a subtle config issue: our health-check readiness timeout default is 60s which lets instances be considered unhealthy during image pull; increasing readiness-probe timeout for heavy images might reduce churn. Adding a patch to AUTOSCALE-299.

autoscale-bot: [info] dispatched emergency config change: dp-42 min_replicas=6 by ida

ida: Next steps (short):
- Monitor p95/p99 for 1h, then decide whether to keep increased min_replicas.
- Continue infra quota push.
- Add warm-pool feature design doc (ENG-PRD).
- Change readiness-probe defaults for GPU images (small runtime patch).

leo: I'll keep AcmeMaps updated. Any objections to offering a small credit for interruption?

maria: Customer appreciated quick action. Approve small credit.

raj: FYI for longer term: consider adding request-level admission control that falls back to cheaper model automatically when queue depth crosses threshold. Ticketed as PRODUCT-112.

ida: Thanks all. I'll leave monitoring on and post final notes in SRE weekly. Closing thread once p99 looks normal for 60m.

leo: Closing update in 30m unless regressions.
